scenes.line1: Why do we need more unit tests?
scenes.say: Why do software teams focus on unit tests? What’s the test pyramid, and why does it matter?
The test pyramid means lots of unit tests at the base, fewer integration tests in the middle, and just a handful of end-to-end tests at the top.

scenes.label: Balance
scenes.sub: More unit tests keep suites fast and reliable.
scenes.say: Balancing test types is key. More unit tests keep your test suite fast and reliable, while fewer E2E tests reduce maintenance headaches.
For example, you might have one hundred unit tests for fast feedback, but only five end-to-end tests since they’re slow and fragile.

scenes.question: Should you write equal numbers of each test?
scenes.right: No. More unit tests, fewer integration, fewest E2E for efficiency.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Should you write equal numbers of each test type? No. More unit tests, fewer integration, and the fewest end-to-end tests maximize efficiency.
